## A force example




## Moments

We calculated (vector) forces using

$$
\mathbf{F}=\int -p(\mathbf{x})\hat{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{x})dA.
$$

To get (vector) moments, we need to fit in the "force $\times$ distance" into the integrand. Well have an infinitesimal force, $-p(\mathbf{x})\hat{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{x})dA$, and we'll use $\mathbf{r}$ as our displacement vector. Remember that when dealing with vectors, torques and moments are actually "distance $\times$ force", and so our integral is

$$
\mathbf{M}=\int -\mathbf{r}\wedge p(\mathbf{x})\hat{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{x})dA
$$

where I used $\wedge$ for the cross product symbol, to make it distinct from $\mathbf{x}$ (which looks like $\times$).
